facts.fact: The vendor's article uses a $1,500 monthly CTV campaign for a local HVAC company as an example, and claims it often outperforms a $1,500 monthly Facebook campaign in lead quality.
facts.quote: This is one of the reasons a $1,500 monthly CTV campaign for a local HVAC company often outperforms a $1,500 Facebook campaign in lead quality.

facts.fact: According to the article, the mere exposure effect was first documented by Robert Zajonc in 1968, a third-party research finding that people develop preferences for things they have seen before.
facts.quote: First documented by Robert Zajonc in 1968, the finding is simple and consistent: people develop preferences for things they've seen before

facts.fact: The article recommends that small businesses run about three to five TV ad impressions per viewer, spaced over a few weeks, to build familiarity; this is the vendor's own guidance, not a measured result.
facts.quote: Three to five impressions, spaced over a few weeks, builds the unconscious familiarity that translates into "I'll call them" when the need arises.

facts.fact: The IAB and most major media buyers settled on 30 seconds as the standard TV ad length.
facts.quote: The IAB and most major media buyers settled on 30 seconds as the standard TV ad length for good reasons rooted in psychology.

facts.fact: Adwave says it standardizes on 30-second TV ads.
facts.quote: This is also why Adwave standardizes on 30 seconds.

facts.fact: Within a 30-second spot, the first 3-5 seconds are pattern recognition, the next 15-20 seconds carry the emotional payload and brand message, and the final 5-7 seconds are the call to action and brand lock-in.
facts.quote: The first 3-5 seconds are pattern recognition (what is this? Is it an ad? Is it relevant to me?).

facts.fact: The emotional payload and brand message occupy the next 15-20 seconds of a 30-second TV spot.
facts.quote: The next 15-20 seconds carry the emotional payload and the brand message.

facts.fact: The call to action and brand lock-in occupy the final 5-7 seconds of a 30-second TV spot.
facts.quote: The final 5-7 seconds are the call to action and brand lock-in.

facts.fact: Most advertising research suggests viewers take action after 3-5 impressions of an ad.
facts.quote: Most advertising research suggests 3-5 impressions before a viewer takes action

facts.fact: Adwave recommends a frequency of 3 to 5 over a few weeks for most small businesses.
facts.quote: For most small businesses, a frequency between 3 and 5 over a few weeks is the sweet spot.

facts.fact: Adwave states that frequency below 2 does not drive enough familiarity.
facts.quote: Frequency below 2 doesn't drive enough familiarity; frequency above 7 starts saturating without producing more conversions.

facts.fact: Adwave states that frequency above 7 starts saturating without producing more conversions.
facts.quote: frequency above 7 starts saturating without producing more conversions.

facts.fact: CTV ad platforms make premium streaming inventory accessible at small business budgets, often starting around $50 in subscription cost.
facts.quote: CTV ad platforms now make premium streaming inventory accessible at small business budgets, often starting around $50 in subscription cost.

facts.fact: The 25-44 demographic is described as one of the heaviest CTV viewing groups.
facts.quote: The 25-44 demographic is one of the heaviest CTV viewing groups and shows the same trust-and-familiarity response patterns.
